page: Amazon Web Services m6a.32xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor system. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 x86_64 processor delivering 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated vCPUs with clock speeds up to 3.6 GHz. System memory comprises 512.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying on networked Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent and ephemeral storage while maintaining a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data reflects strong compute density, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core score of 191,273.61 and a PassMark CPU score of 99,308.37, both positioning within the top 10% tier. Cryptographic capabilities are reinforced by VAES, AES, and SHA_NI hardware extensions, producing a PassMark encryption rating in the top decile. In-memory execution throughput is demonstrated by 129.17 million Redis SET operations per second and cached small-block memory reads reaching 9,076.97 GB/sec. Single-threaded performance sits in the middle 50% across Geekbench and compression tasks, typical of this Zen 3 core architecture.

The absence of local NVMe storage makes this instance dependent on network-attached storage throughput for persistent disk I/O. Furthermore, the processor does not support AVX-512 or AMX matrix instruction sets, constraining high-density deep learning acceleration without dedicated GPUs. With balanced CPU-to-memory allocation and high multi-core scalability, the instance delivers high resource efficiency for horizontally scaled backends, enterprise in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, containerized microservice deployments, and parallel software compilation.

Operating at up to 3.6 GHz, the configuration includes 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server provides 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, omitting bundled local storage and hardware GPU acceleration. Benchmark testing confirms top-tier multi-threaded CPU throughput, scoring 191,273.61 in stress-ng multi-core tests and executing over 129 million Redis SET operations per second. Single-core performance and compression workloads align with median tier metrics. Lacking AVX-512 extensions and local NVMe drives, the m6a.32xlarge is suited for multi-threaded enterprise services, in-memory caching nodes, distributed databases, large-scale Clang compilation, and batch data processing pipelines.
